title: PostgreSQL Enterprise Substrate Audit v1 — Rig Relay
executive_summary: Rig Relay's current data architecture is entirely filesystem-backed (JSONL, JSON, CSV) with DuckDB as the sole in-memory analytical substrate. This is correct for local-first operation and artifact portability, but insufficient for enterprise procurement readiness. Postgres should become the enterprise operational substrate while JSON/JSONL/CSV artifacts remain the portable, schema-governed source of truth.

storage_patterns.role: Disposable analytical substrate for cockpit widgets

storage_patterns.backend: Filesystem (JSON envelopes sharded by envelope_id prefix)
Filesystem (JSON + JSONL) with fcntl advisory locks
storage_patterns.reads_from: Filesystem sessions/, tasks/, leases/paths/, artifacts/, conflicts/ directories
storage_patterns.writes_to: File write + events.jsonl append with fsync

storage_patterns.backend: Filesystem (JSONL read, Markdown write for status updates)
Filesystem (reads JSON files from .build/rig-relay/ and docs/json/)
storage_patterns.reads_from: Various JSON artifacts across build directory and docs tree
storage_patterns.writes_to: Computed projection dict (never persisted directly; sent via WebSocket)

key_observations: Every store is filesystem-backed with JSON/JSONL as canonical format.
DuckDB is the only database component — in-memory, never persisted, acts as a disposable read-side analytical view.
CoordinationStore uses fcntl for cross-process locking — works on same machine, fails across containers.
Report store, findings lifecycle, and receipt store all use linear file scans for querying — O(N) per query.
Projection assembly is entirely reactive (read all files, compute projection, push via WebSocket) — no cache invalidation mechanism.
No tenant isolation, no role-based access, no audit trail for admin operations.
Content-light enforcement exists only at application boundary (events/store.py redact fields), not at storage boundary.

duckdb.role: in-memory analytical queries over JSONL files

httpx.role: useful for Postgres HTTP proxy if needed

pydantic.role: useful for JSONB serialization/validation at boundary

jsonschema.role: useful for JSONB payload validation in CHECK constraints

platformdirs.role: useful for Postgres socket/config path resolution

recommended_additions.justification: psycopg 3 is the modern Postgres adapter. Binary package includes libpq. Preferred over asyncpg for this codebase because: (1) supports both sync and async via psycopg.AsyncConnection, (2) native integration with anyio via async mode, (3) COPY protocol for bulk JSONL ingest, (4) LISTEN/NOTIFY support, (5) connection pool built-in, (6) maintained by Postgres core team. psycopg 3 is the strategic Postgres driver for Python.
recommended_additions.dependency_cost: ~2MB wheel, no system dependencies beyond libpq (included in binary package)

recommended_additions.package: None additional for Phase 0-2 — raw SQL migrations
recommended_additions.justification: Phase 0-2 use raw SQL migration files executed via psycopg. Alembic/SQLAlchemy add ORM overhead and migration lock-in that conflicts with Rig Relay's commitment to raw-SQL transparency. Re-evaluate Alembic at Phase 5 if migration complexity warrants it.

evaluated_and_rejected.reason: Excellent performance but requires a separate event loop integration. psycopg 3 provides comparable performance with better ecosystem integration (anyio-compatible, built-in pool, COPY protocol).

ORM overhead conflicts with Rig Relay's raw-SQL transparency principle. Alembic adds migration framework dependency with its own DSL. Raw SQL migrations are more auditable, portable, and align with Rig Relay's governance culture. Re-evaluate at Phase 5.
Forbidden per existing architecture policy. SQLite is no substitute for Postgres enterprise features (RLS, advisory locks, LISTEN/NOTIFY, logical replication, partitioning, materialized views).

tables.name: artifact_registry
tables.purpose: Registry of all known canonical JSON/JSONL/CSV artifacts with their schema identity, SHA256 hash, and content-light classification
tables.canonical_source_relationship: Read-only index into artifact files. Files remain canonical.
typed_columns: artifact_sha256 CHAR(64) NOT NULL
artifact_path TEXT NOT NULL
artifact_kind TEXT NOT NULL (e.g., 'receipt_envelope', 'release_gate_decision', 'finding', 'event_fabric', 'coordination_event')
schema_id TEXT NOT NULL (references schema_registry.schema_id)
schema_version TEXT NOT NULL
artifact_format TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(artifact_format IN ('json', 'jsonl', 'csv', 'generated_html'))
content_light BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false
secret_bearing BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false
byte_size BIGINT NOT NULL
line_count INTEGER (for JSONL/CSV)
first_observed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
last_validated_at TIMESTAMPTZ
producer TEXT (e.g., 'rig.report', 'tool_invocation', 'coordination_store')
jsonb_columns: metadata JSONB (optional extra metadata: tags, owners, audience, permissions)
indexes: CREATE INDEX idx_artifact_registry_kind ON artifact_registry(artifact_kind)
CREATE INDEX idx_artifact_registry_schema ON artifact_registry(schema_id, schema_version)
CREATE INDEX idx_artifact_registry_content_light ON artifact_registry(content_light) WHERE NOT content_light
CREATE INDEX idx_artifact_registry_path ON artifact_registry USING GIN(to_tsvector('english', artifact_path))
tables.retention_export_policy: Indefinite retention. Artifact registry rows are immutable — insert new row on artifact re-observation with updated hash. Export as CSV for artifact inventory audit.
tables.content_light_guarantees: CHECK(content_light = true OR artifact_kind = 'secret_bearing') — all registered artifacts must declare content_light or secret_bearing classification
tables.replay_export_behavior: Export entire registry as JSONL artifact: .build/rig-relay/enterprise/artifact_registry_export.jsonl

tables.name: artifact_validation
tables.purpose: Validation results for canonical artifacts against their declared JSON Schema
tables.canonical_source_relationship: Read-only log of validation runs. Validation output files remain canonical.
tables.primary_key: validation_id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()
typed_columns: artifact_sha256 CHAR(64) NOT NULL REFERENCES artifact_registry(artifact_sha256)
schema_id TEXT NOT NULL
passed BOOLEAN NOT NULL
error_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
warning_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
validated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
validator_version TEXT
jsonb_columns: errors JSONB (content-light: error messages only, no instance data)
warnings JSONB (content-light: warning messages only)
indexes: CREATE INDEX idx_artifact_validation_hash ON artifact_validation(artifact_sha256)
CREATE INDEX idx_artifact_validation_passed ON artifact_validation(passed) WHERE NOT passed
CREATE INDEX idx_artifact_validation_time ON artifact_validation(validated_at DESC)
tables.retention_export_policy: 90-day retention. Export as CSV for compliance evidence: .build/rig-relay/enterprise/validation_history.csv
tables.content_light_guarantees: errors/warnings JSONB columns contain error messages only — never include the raw JSON instance that failed validation
tables.replay_export_behavior: Export as JSONL: .build/rig-relay/enterprise/validation_export.jsonl

tables.name: event_log
tables.purpose: Operational copy of session observability events for dashboard queries. Envelope-level fields extracted as generated columns from content-light JSONB payload.
tables.canonical_source_relationship: Downstream operational projection. ~/.rig/relay/sessions/<id>/observability.jsonl is canonical.
typed_columns: event_id TEXT NOT NULL
event_name TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'event_name') STORED
session_id TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'session_id') STORED
event_sequence BIGINT GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((payload->>'sequence')::BIGINT) STORED
created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((payload->>'created_at')::TIMESTAMPTZ) STORED
sensitivity_class TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'internal_operational' CHECK(sensitivity_class IN ('public', 'internal_operational', 'telemetry_opt_in', 'redaction_required'))
jsonb_columns: payload JSONB NOT NULL (content-light envelope: event metadata only, no raw prompts/completions/file contents)
indexes: CREATE INDEX idx_event_log_session ON event_log(session_id, created_at DESC)
CREATE INDEX idx_event_log_name ON event_log(event_name, created_at DESC)
CREATE INDEX idx_event_log_payload_gin ON event_log USING GIN(payload jsonb_path_ops)
CREATE INDEX idx_event_log_recent ON event_log(created_at DESC) WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
tables.retention_export_policy: 30-day online retention. Monthly partitions detached and exported as JSONL to cold storage: .build/rig-relay/archive/events/. Can be replayed from canonical observability.jsonl files if cold storage lost.
tables.content_light_guarantees: INSERT trigger: raise exception if payload contains any forbidden key (token, secret, private_key, raw_prompt, raw_completion, file_content, diff, patch)
tables.replay_export_behavior: Export partition as gzipped JSONL artifact: events_2026_05.jsonl.gz

typed_columns: envelope_id TEXT NOT NULL
receipt_kind TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'receipt_kind') STORED
session_id TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'session_id') STORED
created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((payload->>'created_at')::TIMESTAMPTZ) STORED
receipt_sha256 CHAR(64) NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'receipt_sha256') STORED
actor_kind TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->'actor'->>'actor_kind') STORED
subject_kind TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->'subject'->>'subject_kind') STORED
decision_kind TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->'decision'->>'decision_kind') STORED
jsonb_columns: payload JSONB NOT NULL (content-light ReceiptEnvelope.model_dump() output)
indexes: CREATE INDEX idx_receipt_envelope_session ON receipt_envelope(session_id, created_at DESC)
CREATE INDEX idx_receipt_envelope_kind ON receipt_envelope(receipt_kind, created_at DESC)
CREATE INDEX idx_receipt_envelope_actor ON receipt_envelope(actor_kind, subject_kind)

trace_id TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'trace_id') STORED
parent_span_id TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'parent_span_id') STORED
span_kind TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'span_kind') STORED
session_id TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'session_id') STORED
tool_name TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'tool_name') STORED
provider TEXT GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'provider') STORED
started_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((payload->>'started_at')::TIMESTAMPTZ) STORED
duration_ms DOUBLE PRECISION GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((payload->>'duration_ms')::DOUBLE PRECISION) STORED

tables.replay_export_behavior: Can be rebuilt from canonical trace_events.jsonl file.

tables.name: coordination_lease
tables.purpose: Active path reservations and task claims for cross-session coordination. Replaces file-based CoordinationStore for operational hot path.
tables.canonical_source_relationship: Dual authority: Postgres is operational store for active leases. events.jsonl is canonical replay log.
typed_columns: lease_id TEXT NOT NULL
session_id TEXT NOT NULL
task_id TEXT NOT NULL
lease_kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(lease_kind IN ('task_claim', 'path_reservation'))
mode TEXT CHECK(mode IN ('read', 'write'))
status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active' CHECK(status IN ('active', 'released', 'stale', 'expired'))
path_hashes TEXT[] DEFAULT '{}'
ttl_seconds INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 120
created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL
released_at TIMESTAMPTZ
jsonb_columns: scope JSONB (content-light scope definition: allowed_paths hashes only, no raw paths)
indexes: CREATE INDEX idx_coordination_lease_session ON coordination_lease(session_id, status)
CREATE INDEX idx_coordination_lease_active ON coordination_lease(status) WHERE status = 'active'
CREATE INDEX idx_coordination_lease_expires ON coordination_lease(expires_at) WHERE status = 'active'
CREATE INDEX idx_coordination_lease_path ON coordination_lease USING GIN(path_hashes)
tables.retention_export_policy: Released/stale leases archived after 7 days. Active leases retained until released.
tables.content_light_guarantees: path_hashes are salted SHA256 hashes of paths — no raw filesystem paths stored. scope JSONB contains path_hashes and mode only.
tables.replay_export_behavior: All lease operations are also written to events.jsonl for canonical replay.

tables.name: finding
tables.purpose: Operational query surface for out-of-scope findings lifecycle. JSONL remains append-only canonical record.
tables.canonical_source_relationship: Downstream operational projection. docs/findings/out-of-scope-findings.jsonl is canonical.
typed_columns: finding_id TEXT NOT NULL
dedupe_key CHAR(32) NOT NULL
kind TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'kind') STORED
severity TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'severity') STORED CHECK(severity IN ('low', 'medium', 'high', 'critical'))

status TEXT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS (payload->>'status') STORED CHECK(status IN ('open', 'acknowledged', 'triaged', 'accepted', 'deferred', 'blocked', 'in_progress', 'resolved', 'wont_fix', 'superseded', 'duplicate', 'invalid'))
created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((payload->>'created_at')::TIMESTAMPTZ) STORED
updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ GENERATED ALWAYS AS ((payload->>'updated_at')::TIMESTAMPTZ) STORED

ports.signature: Protocol with async methods: register_artifact(ArtifactRef), get_artifact(sha256) -> ArtifactRef, list_by_kind(kind) -> list[ArtifactRef], validate_artifact(sha256, schema_id) -> ValidationResult
Protocol with async methods: ingest_event(event: dict) -> event_id, ingest_batch(events: list[dict]) -> list[str], query_events(filter: EventFilter) -> list[dict]

ports.signature: Protocol (already exists as ReceiptStore in rig_relay/evidence/receipt_store.py): append(envelope) -> Path, get(envelope_id) -> ReceiptEnvelope, list(...), list_by_session(...), count()
ports.postgres_adapter: PostgresReceiptStore implements ReceiptStore protocol. append() writes to Postgres AND filesystem (dual authority). get() reads from Postgres. list() uses indexed queries.

ports.signature: Protocol with async methods: claim_task(...), reserve_paths(...), release_paths(...), publish_artifact(...), report_conflict(...), read_state_projection()
ports.postgres_adapter: PostgresCoordinationStore implements same API. Uses pg_advisory_lock() instead of fcntl. Maintains dual writes to events.jsonl for canonical replay.

ports.signature: Protocol with async methods: get_latest_projection(kind) -> Projection, invalidate_projection(kind, reason) -> None, subscribe_invalidation(kinds: list[str]) -> AsyncIterator[InvalidationEvent]

ports.signature: Protocol with async methods: compute_aggregate(kind, period_start, period_end) -> Aggregate, refresh_materialized_view(view_name) -> None, query_dashboard(widget_id) -> list[dict]
ports.postgres_adapter: PostgresTelemetryProjection computes aggregates in Postgres, refreshes materialized views, and returns dashboard query results.

ports.signature: Protocol with async methods: run_migrations(target_version: str) -> MigrationReport, validate_migration_consistency() -> bool, get_migration_history() -> list[MigrationRecord]
ports.existing_module_dependency: New module. No existing migration infrastructure.
ports.postgres_adapter: PostgresMigrationRunner executes raw SQL migration files in order, uses advisory lock for exclusive migration access.

ports.signature: Protocol with async methods: export_table_to_artifact(table_name) -> ExportManifest, replay_from_artifact(artifact_path) -> ReplayVerification, verify_export_equivalence(table_name) -> bool
ports.existing_module_dependency: New module. No existing export infrastructure.
ports.postgres_adapter: PostgresExportReplay exports tables to JSONL via COPY TO, verifies SHA256 equivalence between exported artifacts and canonical source artifacts.

interface_port_strategy.adapter_registration: All adapters registered via a lightweight registry pattern consistent with rig_relay/provider_registry/. Adapters are lazy-loaded — Postgres adapters only initialized when Postgres connection string is configured. File-based adapters remain the default for local-first operation.

phases.name: Schema Contracts
phases.description: JSON Schema contracts for Postgres projection manifests. Defines the interface between artifact authority and Postgres operational projections.
phases.deliverable: docs/schemas/rig.relay.postgres_*.v1.schema.json files. Migration SQL files generated from schemas.

phases.name: File-backed Reference Adapter
phases.description: Implement all Port interfaces with file-backed reference adapters. FilesystemReceiptStore already implements ReceiptStore. Create FileArtifactRegistry, FileProjectionStore, etc. All adapters produce equivalent results.
phases.deliverable: Working port interfaces + file-backed adapters + contract tests

phases.name: Postgres Adapter
phases.description: Implement Postgres adapters behind same ports. Create migration runner. Postgres schema created from Phase 1 migration SQL.
phases.deliverable: Working Postgres adapters + migration runner + integration tests

phases.name: Replay Equivalence Tests
phases.description: Verify file-backed adapter and Postgres adapter produce equivalent semantic projections when consuming the same canonical artifact corpus.
phases.deliverable: Equivalence test suite passing. Real artifact fixtures.

phases.name: Cockpit Integration
phases.description: Desktop cockpit uses ProjectionStorePort for projections instead of ad-hoc projection blob assembly. LISTEN/NOTIFY for real-time projection invalidation.
phases.deliverable: Cockpit queries Postgres materialized views. WebSocket invalidation via NOTIFY channels.

phases.name: Enterprise Mode
phases.description: When enterprise mode is enabled (Postgres connection string configured), Postgres becomes operational substrate. File-backends remain available for local mode. Dual-write ensures canonical artifacts are always exported.
phases.deliverable: Enterprise mode toggle. Export manager running periodic artifact exports. Admin dashboard.

phases.name: Procurement Documentation
phases.description: Backup/restore runbooks, admin query cookbook, retention policy documentation, incident investigation guides, tenant provisioning guides.

telemetry_operational_state_boundary.principle: Postgres enterprise substrate is not merely analytics. Postgres owns operational queryability, projection invalidation, audit/event correlation, enterprise admin debuggability, and replay/export orchestration. Product telemetry is a separate policy layer that must not be conflated with operational correctness or enterprise evidence continuity.
postgres_roles: Postgres is the enterprise operational substrate, not merely an analytics engine.
Postgres owns operational queryability of receipts, events, leases, findings, and audit records.
Postgres owns projection invalidation via LISTEN/NOTIFY — an operational mechanism, not a telemetry mechanism.
Postgres owns enterprise admin debuggability and audit/event correlation.
Postgres owns replay/export orchestration through ExportReplayPort.
artifact_roles: JSON/JSONL/CSV remain the portable, diffable, replayable, schema-governed source-of-truth artifacts.
Artifacts are the canonical authority for all content-bearing data.
DuckDB remains the disposable analytical microscope for ad-hoc queries over local artifact files.
DuckDB does not replace Postgres for operational dashboards, cockpit widgets, or audit queries.

product_telemetry_disabled.description: Product-learning telemetry is disabled. Adaptive features (Ralph ranking, orchestrator refinement, suggested tool sequences) visibly degrade. Remote contribution and cross-user aggregate intelligence are offline.
product_telemetry_disabled.what_must_not_happen: Receipt persistence, mutation receipts, release-gate decisions, schema validation records, export manifests, enterprise audit events, content-light incident investigation records, or Postgres operational substrate features must NOT stop or degrade.
product_telemetry_disabled.what_is_affected: Product-learning analytics, adaptive recommendations, cross-org aggregate telemetry, hosted product-learning dashboards.
product_telemetry_disabled.cockpit_status: product_telemetry_disabled — info-level indicator. Not an error.

postgres_unavailable.description: Postgres is configured (RIG_RELAY_POSTGRES_DSN is set) but unreachable (connection refused, timeout, auth failure).
postgres_unavailable.what_must_happen: Fail-closed. Adapters raise PostgresUnavailableError. Cockpit shows 'Enterprise substrate unavailable' degradation state. No silent fallback to file-backed adapters. No data written to Postgres.
postgres_unavailable.what_is_affected: All Postgres-dependent operations: event_log ingestion, receipt_envelope queries, coordination_lease acquisition, projection invalidation via LISTEN/NOTIFY, enterprise audit event writes.

local_diagnostics_disabled.description: Local operational observability is explicitly disabled via a separate local_diagnostics setting (distinct from product telemetry consent).
local_diagnostics_disabled.what_is_affected: Local event collection, trace spans, cockpit health metrics. Audit/evidence tables may still be intact if enterprise mode is enabled.

telemetry_operational_state_boundary.non_conflation_rule: Telemetry-disabled mode must not be confused with Postgres-unavailable mode. Product telemetry-disabled is degraded-but-operational. Postgres-unavailable in enterprise mode is fail-closed. Local diagnostics-disabled is distinct from both. Cockpit must surface these as separately distinguishable states.

remaining_seams.description: PostgresCoordinationStore must maintain dual writes to events.jsonl for canonical replay. If Postgres write succeeds but file write fails (or vice versa), the two authorities diverge.
remaining_seams.mitigation: Write to Postgres first, then write to events.jsonl. If events.jsonl write fails, mark Postgres row as 'pending_replay' and retry with exponential backoff. Monitor for drift via coordination integrity check.

remaining_seams.description: During Phase 2-4, DuckDB reads from raw JSONL while Postgres reads from operational tables. Schema migration or data transformation could cause divergence in computed projections.
remaining_seams.mitigation: Phase 4 equivalence tests must run on every commit. Projection comparison test fetches same widget from both DuckDB and Postgres and asserts strict equality on content-light fields.

remaining_seams.description: If Postgres connection drops between NOTIFY and LISTEN processing, projection invalidation events are lost. Cockpit shows stale data.
remaining_seams.mitigation: ProjectionStorePort.subscribe_invalidation() must detect connection loss and trigger a full projection recomputation on reconnect. Projection TTL (30-300 seconds depending on widget) provides safety net.

remaining_seams.description: If Postgres is configured but unreachable, all adapters must fail closed, not silently degrade to file-backed modes. Silently falling back to file backends would hide Postgres infrastructure issues.
remaining_seams.mitigation: Adapters raise PostgresUnavailableError with clear diagnostics. Cockpit shows 'Enterprise substrate unavailable' degradation state. Local mode disables all Postgres features.

remaining_seams.description: Generated columns are STORED — they recalculate on INSERT/UPDATE only. If an application updates the JSONB column without explicitly setting the generated column, the two diverge.
remaining_seams.mitigation: All writes go through typed INSERT statements that explicitly set both JSONB and source values. No direct JSONB-only updates. Migration tests validate generated column values match JSONB source.
